text:
maria_g: Quick follow-up from last night's outage — we need to update the PRD for multi-tenant fallback behavior. Can we agree on a narrowed scope so we can ship safe guardrails this sprint?

jamal_k: +1. What are you proposing we cut vs keep for the MVP?

maria_g: Proposal: 1) MVP = deterministic fallback to smaller model + region failover, 2) defer dynamic cost-based routing and per-tenant weighting to v2, 3) include safety throttles and a kill-switch. Acceptance criteria attached at a high level.

olivia_s: From SRE: must include automatic rollback if L99 latency > 1.2s for 5m and error rate > 0.5% for 3m. Also require a playbook entry for manual override.

jamal_k: Technical acceptance criteria I want captured: - Fallback path maintained under KV-cache semantics (no hallucination regressions) - end-to-end latency added by fallback < 200ms median - tests: synthetic cross-tenant spike + cached-prefix tests.

maria_g: Good. I'll add those to the PRD. Also adding a customer-facing constraint: AcmeCorp requires no data from premium tenants routed through shared queues during fallback.

devon_p: Sales flagged AcmeCorp as negotiable only if we can guarantee isolation in the short-term. Suggest we present a scope trade: deliver guardrails + transparent SLA language now, roadmap the per-tenant isolation feature with timeline.

jamal_k: For implementation, here's the simplest policy snippet I used in staging:
```
# fallback policy (pseudo-config)
fallback: 
  trigger: latency > 1.0s or model_error_rate > 0.3%
  action: route_to_variant: small-llm-v1
  preserve_kv_cache: true
  isolation: tenant-pinned-queues (opt in)
```

olivia_s: +1 to the config. Add alerts: trigger paging if fallback persists > 10m and throughput > 70% of baseline.

maria_g: For the PRD text, acceptance criteria bullets I'll include: - functional: fallback activates and returns responses with token-similarity >= 95% to primary in test prompts - reliability: no SLA penalties for customers under fallback if isolation enforced - observability: trace-level correlation between fallback events and tenant IDs - rollback: canary deploys with 1% traffic ramp then 10% then full, auto-rollback on SLO breach.

devon_p: Timeline? PM ask from sales: ship guardrails + updated SLA language as hotfix by end of next week, roadmap notes for per-tenant isolation in Q2.

jamal_k: Engineering note: can do the basic routing + cache preservation in 2w if we cut the cost-routing piece. Need one person on infra for queue pinning.

olivia_s: Runbook updates we need: step-by-step for manual fallback toggle, how to interpret fallback traces, who to page for persistent fallback (oncall, infra lead), and a short checklist for post-event RCA correlation keys.

maria_g: I'll draft the PRD update and inline acceptance criteria today and tag you all for review. Will also add a minimal runbook patch that SRE can iterate on.

jamal_k: Quick call? 10-min sync in 15 to lock scope and owners.

devon_p: On it — grabbing calendar.

deploy-bot: Incident #234: deployment rollback executed at 1835041200, service restored. Logs: https://internal.redwood/incident/234 :eyes:

olivia_s: Thanks — that rollback signal is helpful for timeline in the PRD.

maria_g: Decision summary (to be added to PRD): 1) Narrow MVP to deterministic fallback + region failover + kill-switch 2) Add SRE acceptance criteria (latency/error thresholds + paging) 3) Add customer isolation note for AcmeCorp and flag per-tenant isolation as Q2 deliverable 4) Rollout plan: canary -> auto-rollback on SLO breaches 5) Runbook patch to land with PRD update. :shipit:

jamal_k: Ack. I'll start the draft PR and link tech details.

devon_p: I'll coordinate with sales on messaging and get AcmeCorp sign-off ASAP.

maria_g: Thanks everyone — tagging action items in the PRD draft in ~30m.
